response.justification: The candidate is a highly experienced, versatile engineer (15+ years) with strong software craftsmanship, testing, and distributed/event-driven systems background, but the core requirement of this role — deep, current C++/STL expertise for high-performance industrial automation platforms — is largely absent. C++ exposure is limited to roughly seven months at National Instruments in 2014–2015 and a university thesis project; C++ does not even appear in the listed skills. There is no evidence of IEC 62443/SDL secure engineering, MQTT/IoT industrial protocols (Modbus, OPC UA, IEC 61850), Azure, or automation-industry domain knowledge. The low-latency D/Node.js work and event-driven GIS platform show relevant architectural instincts, but retraining onto a C++ industrial-cybersecurity stack would be substantial. Better suited to a full-stack or platform engineering role.
strengths: Deep experience with high-throughput, low-latency, event-driven distributed systems
Strong engineering discipline: TDD, CI/CD, mentoring, open-source tooling and public talks
Broad multi-language, full-stack and embedded exposure with fast adaptability
concerns: Minimal and dated hands-on C++/STL experience (~7 months, 2014–2015)
No industrial automation, IEC 62443/SDL, or OT protocol (MQTT, OPC UA, Modbus) background
Career trajectory is web/cloud full-stack, not systems-level performance engineering
